name: org.machanism.machai:gw-mcp-server
description: Ghostwriter MCP Server is an executable Java 17 Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that combines Ghostwriter project-aware code-assistance workflows with Bindex Core metadata retrieval, registration, semantic discovery, and library recommendation capabilities. It exposes these workflows through the Machai MCP Server runtime for MCP clients, IDE integrations, and developer-automation processes. The executable entry point is org.machanism.machai.mcp.server.McpServer. Launching without a port uses the STDIO transport; --port enables an HTTP server and --session enables streamable HTTP sessions. The server accepts a project directory, name, and advertised version, and its Ghostwriter model-assisted workflows use the configured generative-AI provider and model. The Maven artifact depends on Ghostwriter, Bindex Core, and Machai MCP Server and is packaged as a runnable JAR.

constructors.description: Creates the MCP server entry-point object. Operational startup is normally performed through the static main method in the assembled executable JAR.

examples.description: Creates the documented entry-point object. For an MCP deployment, launch the executable JAR so the runtime manages the selected transport.

features.name: main
features.signature: public static void main(java.lang.String[] args) throws java.lang.Exception
features.description: Starts the unified Ghostwriter and Bindex MCP tool server. No port option selects STDIO transport; -p or --port starts HTTP mode; -s or --session enables streamable HTTP mode.

examples.description: Starts a named server in STDIO mode for a local MCP client and supplies the current project directory to project-aware workflows.
Starts a streamable HTTP MCP server on port 45000 for an HTTP-capable MCP client.

features.name: getConfigurator
features.signature: public static org.machanism.macha.core.commons.configurator.PropertiesConfigurator getConfigurator(java.lang.String configFile) throws java.io.IOException
features.description: Creates the properties configurator and loads the requested configuration file. A null configFile uses the default MCP configuration and tolerates its absence; an explicitly requested unreadable file causes java.io.IOException.

examples.description: Loads an explicitly named server properties file before startup. The file must contain valid runtime and AI-provider settings.

customizations.name: MCP command-line transport options
customizations.description: Use -p or --port to select HTTP mode, -s or --session to enable streamable HTTP mode, -d or --projectDir for the project path, -n or --name for the server name, -v or --version for the advertised version, and -h or --help for usage information. Without a port, the server uses STDIO.

examples.description: Configures a project directory and server name, then starts streamable HTTP mode on port 45000.

customizations.name: Ghostwriter AI model configuration
customizations.description: The effective Maven build configures gw.model as CodeMie:gpt-5.6-luna-2026-07-09. Configure provider credentials and connection settings outside source control through the Ghostwriter or Machai runtime configuration.

examples.description: Sets the provider-qualified model identifier used by Ghostwriter model-assisted workflows.

examples.name: Build, configure, and launch a local STDIO MCP server
steps: From the project root, build the runnable artifact with mvn clean install -Ppack.
Configure the CodeMie credentials and required runtime connection settings outside source control. Set gw.model=CodeMie:gpt-5.6-luna-2026-07-09 if an explicit model selection is needed.
Configure an MCP client to start java -jar target/gw-mcp-server-1.4.2.jar --projectDir ..
Start the MCP client. With no port argument, it communicates with the server over standard input and output.
Use the discovered Ghostwriter project workflows or Bindex metadata workflows for the selected project.
examples.description: This local-process scenario lets an IDE or AI assistant manage Ghostwriter MCP Server through the STDIO transport.

examples.name: Run a streamable HTTP MCP server
steps: Build the project with mvn clean install -Ppack.
Prepare the AI-provider runtime configuration when model-assisted workflows are required.
Start the server with java -jar target/gw-mcp-server-1.4.2.jar --projectDir . --port 45000 --session.
Configure an HTTP-capable MCP client to connect to the host and port where the server is running.
Connect the client and invoke the advertised Ghostwriter or Bindex tools for the target project.
examples.description: This scenario exposes the same MCP capabilities through HTTP and enables streamable sessions.

examples.name: Declare the server artifact in a Maven application
steps: Add the displayed dependency to the application's pom.xml.
Resolve the artifact from Maven Central or make it available in the local Maven repository.
When embedding is intentional, invoke org.machanism.machai.mcp.server.McpServer.main from the hosting application; otherwise prefer the standalone JAR for process isolation.
examples.description: This dependency declaration supports applications that intentionally embed the server entry point.
